correctness.rationale: For any four nonnegative zero gaps, palindromic scattered subsequences are partitioned by their zero, one, two or three occurrences of symbol one. A union of the first/third pair rectangle and at most one excess rectangle gives the two-one term, with full intersection control. Three-one palindromes form an independent integer rectangle, and one-one palindromes form the union of three nested initial intervals. The restricted symmetric-source maximum is obtained by a strictly concave quadratic with uniquely closest admissible integer vertex. The exact checker freshly validates 1,820 candidate-enumeration cases and 7,315 independent interval-DP cases, and the unique symmetric maximizer for 101 half-gap sums; these checks corroborate, not replace, the proof.

value.rationale: Three-marker sparse words are a natural first class where palindromic scattered subsequences of every one-count occur, and their precise gap dependence is not encoded by the all-subsequence total. The constant-time exact identity identifies the sole nontrivial overlap correction and all boundary cases; it simultaneously yields a nontrivial unique all-length extremal classification among palindromic source words. This structural result is more than a finite table or naive parameter substitution. No unrestricted optimum is claimed.
